newsitem.title: USA: Clinton signs law to protect tax confidentiality.
newsitem.headline: Clinton signs law to protect tax confidentiality.

text.p: President Clinton on Tuesday signed into law legislation to protect the confidentiality of tax returns filed with the Internal Revenue Service (IRS).

Clinton said in a statement, released by the White House, that the law provides new criminal penalties for those who view tax information without authorisation, a practice known as browsing, as well as additional civil remedies for people whose privacy is violated.
Under current law it is illegal to intentionally use a federal computer without authority so as to obtain information from any government department.

The "Taxpayer Browsing Protection Act" signed into law on Tuesday would also make it a misdemeanor to make unauthorised inspections of non-computerized tax information, such as "hard copies" of tax returns.
The new law also makes it easier for people to seek civil remedies if their privacy has been violated by such browsing.
